name: BACH_0306
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (88%)** · Ambiguous: Normal vs Benign · Careful review
Conformal set holds Normal and Benign; invasive probability is under 1% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 88%, Normal 11% | Benign leads, Normal second |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.89 / 64th percentile | Image looks typical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign | Weak neighbor support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 8, 9, 10) · ↓ invasive · Strongest concept term (−1.30); scored above typical · Unreliable (0/20) [F2]
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 0, 10) · ↓ invasive · Term −0.22; associated with lower invasive likelihood · Validated (20/20)
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↑ invasive · Small positive term (+0.18) against the benign call · Validated (19/20)
- **Immune cell fraction** (regions 1, 10, 11) · context · 22% of nuclei; top of reference range · Measured [F7]

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions cut the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Two of five nearest reference cases are InSitu; the model's set excludes InSitu but neighbors disagree.
- Nuclei were segmented in only 3 regions, flagged insufficient tumor nuclei, so cell measures are sparse.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 8, 9, 10:** Confirm two-layered lobular epithelium; the concept score failed its spot check.
2. **Region 3:** Look for infiltrating tumor in stroma; this region peaks for that concept.
3. **Regions 1, 10, 11:** Judge whether the dense immune infiltrate is reactive or accompanies a lesion.
